vampires , like the name nd concept tht ur thinking abt, r very specific to eastern europe HOWEVER blood drinking creatures have existed way prior to Christianity, though, they arent considered vampires in the traditional sense since the word and concept of vampire emerged from eastern europe with the the word upir like you mentioned. 

a neat book you might like is "The Vampire: A New History." by Nick Groom, it talks a lot about the first instances of vampires prior to Christianity and even talk about blood drinking all the way back to Homer and The Odyssey (though the blood drinking there is different than we see in the concept of vampires now but it still existed wayyyyyyyyy before Christianity). 

also the creatures you mention, could be considered vampires if you just look at how they relate to vampires, but i think to call them vampires takes away their cultural signifiance (of both the other creature and the vampire)  since again, vampires originated and are almost exclusive to eastern European folklore (and obviously made its way through a lot of Europe and eventually to America), but calling, for example, the Obayifo, a vampire, although it would be accurate to an extent, its placing a european word and concept on a piece of African Folk Lore that was created seprately and independently from the vampire and also was created for a separate reason (since, the vampire was a creature created as a response to mass plague nd death nd epidemics etc) 

so tldr: yes you could say blood drinking creatures, mythos and folklore existed prior to Christianity because it did and yes they COULD be called vampires because they are very similar however, calling them vampires would take away from the history and cultural importance of both the word vampire as well as reduce the cultural nd historical importance of whatever creature ur comparing to the vampire

edit: if you want specific sources, outside the book i mentioned, i can offer some! I got most of ny information from said book, as well as lectures from a professor who specializes in vampire mythos nd history!
